description: The closed alert `kind` enum (Phase 7 §10, pulled forward from the P9-D plan). `kinds` is the full enum every consumer must recognize; the remaining lists partition it by single-writer ownership: the flow monitor raises AND auto-resolves `monitor_kinds` (pipeline/flow/monitor.py MONITOR_KINDS), the notify module owns `notify_kinds` (pipeline/notify/repo.py WEBHOOK_FAILED_KIND), and `declared_kinds` is the enum's waiting room — kinds that exist for labelling and cross-runtime agreement but have NO writer yet. The app's EXPECTATION_BREACH_KIND branch and the monitoring UI's kind labels pin against `kinds`. Phase 9 (M5-0) declared the three process kinds in `declared_kinds`; M5-E claimed all three for the monitor, because each is evaluated as a CONDITION observed from state (a dead run, a deferred run, a breached per-source expectation) rather than raised at the moment it happens — which is exactly what makes auto-resolve fall out of the condition's absence. `declared_kinds` stays as the mechanism for the next kind whose writer is not yet decided. C-1 (container-images spec §10) declared `process_image_flagged` (one open alert per process whose CURRENT revision references an image that is flagged, revoked or stale); C-4 moved it to its own writer list, `image_kinds` (pipeline/images/alerts.py IMAGE_ALERT_KINDS), which reconciles through sync_alerts scoped to that list. `declared_kinds` is empty and stays as the waiting room. The partition order is monitor, image, declared, notify.
